background_notes.fact: For gamma>0 and a real mean-zero f in H^gamma(Torus), the symmetric Fourier truncations f_m=Ple_m f, m positive integer, are smooth real mean-zero trigonometric polynomials with ||f_m||_(H^gamma)<=||f||_(H^gamma). Moreover ||f||_2<=||f||_(H^gamma), ||f_m||_2<=||f||_(H^gamma), and f_m tends to f in H^gamma and hence in L2.

grounds.reason: L1 supplies the real mean-zero datum in H^gamma with norm at most R and defines its truncations.
Gives the weighted Fourier norm, its completion, and the meanings of real and mean-zero.

background_notes.justification: The retained frequencies form a finite set, so their inverse Fourier sum is smooth. The symmetric indicator preserves coefficient conjugacy and the zero coefficient. Removing nonnegative terms contracts the squared H^gamma norm. Since (1+k^2)^gamma>=1, the L2 norm is dominated by that norm (and this bounded inclusion extends to the completion). The squared H^gamma approximation error is the tail sum over |k|>m of the convergent nonnegative weighted Fourier series, which tends to zero; L2 convergence follows by domination.

background_notes.fact: If x_m tends to x in a normed subspace X and F:X->X is continuous, then for any fixed nonnegative integer j, F iterated j times at x_m tends to F iterated j times at x. In this packet X is the real mean-zero L2 space and F=Psi_tau for the fixed tau>0.

grounds.reason: Supplies convergent initial truncations and tau=T/Lsteps>0 under L1.
Psi_tau is continuous on X and preserves X.
Identifies the numerical trajectories with finite iterations of the same Psi_tau.

background_notes.justification: For j=0 this is the initial convergence. If convergence holds at j, continuity at F iterated j times at x sends that convergent sequence to the required limit at j+1, by the epsilon-delta definition of continuity. Induction supplies every j up to the fixed finite Lsteps; preservation ensures each continuity application lies in X.

background_notes.fact: In a normed space, if a_m^n tends to a^n and b_m^n tends to b^n for every n in a fixed finite nonempty index set, and ||a_m^n-b_m^n||<=B for every m,n with fixed real B, then max_n ||a^n-b^n||<=B.

grounds.reason: F002 provides the common bound B=C*tau^gamma for all approximating trajectories.
F003 provides both convergences at every grid point.
L1 fixes a positive integer Lsteps, so n=0,...,Lsteps is a finite nonempty set.

background_notes.justification: The triangle inequality gives | ||a_m^n-b_m^n||-||a^n-b^n|| | <= ||a_m^n-a^n||+||b_m^n-b^n||, whose right side tends to zero. The limit therefore remains <=B at each n: a larger limit would contradict convergence with epsilon half its excess over B. Taking the maximum of the finitely many resulting inequalities yields the assertion.
